text:
maya: Heads up — saw autoscaler oscillation in us-west-2 around 09:12UTC. The headroom panel in Grafana shows short-lived dips (~20-40s) that trigger scale-ups then immediate scale-downs. Feels like noise in the queue metric.
jon: Link? screenshot?
maya: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/headroom?orgId=1&from=now-1h&to=now — see the blue spikes under 0.2 headroom repeated 6x. Query currently used for panel:
```
avg_over_time(redwood_inference_queue_length{env="prod",region="us-west-2"}[1m])
```
looks like it's very sensitive to transient bursts when batch size is small.
liam: i've been meaning to say we should smooth that query. try avg_over_time(...[5m]) or use 'max_over_time' for the short tail. e.g.:
```
max_over_time(avg_over_time(redwood_inference_queue_length{env="prod"}[1m])[5m:])
```
That will avoid promoting on 10-20s blips.
jon: also alerts currently fire with evaluation 1m and no 'for'. That guarantees flapping. Recommend adding 'for: 5m' and bumping evaluation interval to 1m to 30s step for Prometheus recording rules.
maya: another angle — we have standby GPUs in the pool (metric: redwood_standby_gpu_count). Autoscaler treats them as available but our panel doesn't show them. If a scale-up would only flip standby->active, we should prefer that vs spinning up new capacity. Can we add standby to panel and to the scaler decision? (it already exists in the scaler, but the panel/o11y should show it)
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] scale-controller v2 deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T09:05:12Z :rocket:
srebot: Alert: autoscaler_high_churn firing in us-west-2 (3x) — see incident #INC-2241
liam: proposal: 1) introduce a recording rule for smoothed headroom:
```
# in prometheus/rules.yaml
record: cluster:headroom_smoothed:avg5m
expr: avg_over_time((capacity_gpus - used_gpus - reserved_gpus - inferred_pending_gpus)[5m])
```
2) use that record in Grafana + in autoscaler decision logic. 3) change alert to use 'for: 5m' and trigger on p95 headroom < 0.25 rather than instantaneous avg.
jon: agree. also add a panel that shows batch size distribution (p50/p90/p99) per model — we've seen tiny batches spike queues even though overall throughput is low. If batch size median < 8, treat small bursts differently.
maya: cost note: with current churn we estimate ~2.4k USD/month extra from short-lived scale-ups in us-west-2 (ballpark based on recent billing + per-gpu-minute). If we can reduce false-positive scale-ups by 60-70% that’s meaningful.
liam: will open a PR with the recording rule + dashboard updates. Can someone own the canary in eu-west-1? We should roll the new panel and alert rules there first.
maya: i'll own the eu-west-1 canary. i'll also add a runbook entry: how to pause autoscaler and force standby promotion in emergency.
Action items:
- liam: PR with recording rule + grafana panel changes (tag: ops/autoscale-headroom)
- maya: canary rollout in eu-west-1 + runbook update
- jon: update alert 'for' and evaluation interval in prom-alerts
Thanks — i'll post the PR link once ready. :thumbsup:
jon: SGTM, thanks maya/liam.
maya: marking follow-ups in Jira: INF-983 (dashboard), INF-984 (alert tuning), INF-985 (runbook).
